source.author: verg
source.text: hunc tibi praeterea, spes et solacia nostri, Pallanta adiungam; sub te tolerare magistro militiam et grave Martis opus, tua cernere facta assuescat primis et te miretur ab annis.
source.text_original: hunc tibi praeterea, spes et solacia nostri, / Pallanta adiungam; sub te tolerare magistro / militiam et grave Martis opus, tua cernere facta / assuescat primis et te miretur ab annis.
source.text_english: Moreover, I shall attach to you this Pallas, hope and comfort of us, so that under you as his teacher he may learn to endure soldiering and the hard work of Mars, to behold your deeds from his earliest years, and to admire you from his childhood.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: Haemoniam primis Pelias frenabat ab annis, iam gravis et longus populis metus: illius amnes Ionium quicumque petunt, ille Othryn et Haemum atque imum felix versabat vomere Olympum.
reuse.text_original: Haemoniam primis Pelias frenabat ab annis, / iam gravis et longus populis metus: illius amnes / Ionium quicumque petunt, ille Othryn et Haemum / atque imum felix versabat vomere Olympum.
reuse.text_english: From his earliest years Pelias was restraining Haemonia, now a heavy and long-standing fear to the peoples: for all its rivers that seek the Ionian Sea, he ploughed Othrys and Haemus and even the lowliest slopes of Olympus with his happy plow.
